newsitem.title: USA: U.S. close to settlement for radiation victims.
newsitem.headline: U.S. close to settlement for radiation victims.

text.p: Families of 12 victims of secret radiation tests are close to securing a $4.8 million settlement with the government, a lawyer for the families said Friday.

The settlement would be the first since the Clinton administration promised a year ago that it would compensate people harmed by the government's Cold War-era radiation tests, which in many cases were conducted without their consent.
"These were the most horrendous of the cases," said Ray Heslin of New York law firm Gold, Farrell and Marks, one of the group's attorneys.
Papers on the $4.8 million settlement, which would be divided equally, are set to be handed over to the government Monday, he said, confirming reports in the Miami Herald and Washington Post.
Administration officials declined to comment on the specific cases. An Energy Department spokeswoman said only that "it's an ongoing negotiation."
The settlement would cover 12 out of 18 people who were injected with plutonium or uranium at the University of Rochester and University of Chicago.
Only one of the victims, Mary Jean Connell, was believed to be still alive. She was injected with uranium salts about 50 years ago when she was in her 20s, Heslin said.
The experiments, which were done to study the potential effects of nuclear fallout, appeared to have caused bone damage in at least some cases, based on autopsies done in the 1970s.
"Their bones actually look like Swiss cheese," said Heslin, describing the autopsy results.
Other lawsuits against the government are still pending, including one involving prisoners in Oregon seeking $250 million in damages.

An administration official said President Clinton was eager to close the books on the Cold War experiments. "We're very sensitive to not just what some of these actions did to the individual families, but what it does to people's trust in government," said the administration official, who asked not to be named.
